_comment: Diet engine quality baseline. Re-recorded because the CATALOGUE the gate measures against was wrong, not because the engine changed direction. FoodCategory.by_canonical_name used `Q(name_en=label) | Q(name=label)`, and modeltranslation rewrites the second arm to `name_en` as well, so a category row written before the translation columns existed was invisible: the INSERT that followed hit UNIQUE(name), the retry re-ran the same blind query, and the method returned None. `load_food_catalogue` assigned that None. Measured on the gate's own database: 86 of 136 foods came out of a rebuild with NO category, three categories had no English name and two were missing entirely, and `classify_food` fell back to guessing a food's macro role from its numbers. Every figure recorded before this describes that database. On the corrected one the engine serves richer plates: dish rate 0.792 -> 0.804, chosen-ingredient share 0.239 -> 0.307, preference satisfaction 0.625 -> 0.688, twin identical meals 1 -> 0, per-client weekly repeats 4 -> 3. Distinct dishes 63 -> 60 and worst calorie drift 2.57 -> 3.33 move the other way: a six-line dinner is harder to portion than a four-line one, which is also why the optimiser gained a three-at-once move (see diet/planner/optimize.py for the measured trade-off table). Two earlier deliberate trades still hold: a substitution may not replace the ingredient a dish is named after, and candidate ORDER is bounded below the value of an explicit choice. min_distinct_portions_per_food is measured over engine-BUILT plates only, because a recipe author's pinned clove of garlic is meant to be identical every time.
